title: The Presentation of Christ
english: The feast of the meeting of our Lord Jesus Christ is a celebration that surpasses all others, for it is a sabbath of sabbaths, a holy of holies, where the whole mystery of the incarnation of Christ is summed up, and the whole appearance of the only-begotten Son is described.

This feast commemorates the presentation of Christ in the temple, where he was carried in arms and confessed as God, and where a pair of turtledoves was offered to Simeon and Anna, as the evangelical words are interwoven with the history of the feast.

According to the law of Moses, every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord (Leviticus 12:2), and a sacrifice shall be offered, according to what was said in the law of the Lord, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Leviticus 12:8).
Our Lord, who served for us, ought to have offered purification for us, and he did so, not sparing the pair of turtledoves, just as he did not spare his own blood.

When the days of their purification were fulfilled according to Moses' law, the question arises as to whose purification is being referred to, since Joseph was neither the father nor the one responsible for the purification, and neither Mary nor the child needed purification.
The scripture states that a woman who conceives and bears a male is unclean for seven days (Leviticus 12:2), but Mary did not conceive by seed, and therefore, she did not need purification.
The scripture also states that if a woman gives birth to a female, she is unclean for twice seven days (Leviticus 12:5).
Eve gave birth to a weak vessel, the broken pottery, the bacteria of the disease, the hand of disobedience, the counselor of the dragon, and the frailty introduced through her.

However, just as we have heard of the woman's transgressions, we must also learn of her achievements, for the Theotokos introduced virginity to life, carried God in her womb, and gave birth to Him in the flesh, renewing our race.

She was the first to receive Jesus from the dead, the first to proclaim the resurrection, and the first to announce joy to the disciples; her field was not a virgin vineyard that did not undergo the plow, so the offering was not for her but for the whole race.

Christ's actions are undertaken for our sake: he is circumcised, baptized for us, and the purifications of the law are fulfilled on our behalf; if he weeps, he washes away nature; if he is struck, he frees our captivity; if he carries the cross, he lightens us of the yoke of sin; and if he is spat upon, he delivers Adam from the spittle of the curse.
As the lawgiver, Christ fulfills his own law beyond the requirements of the law, leaving the gate of the virgin closed, and not breaking the seal that was set upon it.
baehrens: PG 93; Homilia i de Hypapante (Khazarzar) u01 open
translator_notes: The Greek contains the direct quotation 'ὅτι πᾶν ἄρσεν διανοῖγον μήτραν ἅγιον τῷ κυρίῳ κληθήσεται' which is rendered in English as 'every male opening the womb shall be called holy to the Lord'.
The Greek contains the direct quotation 'ζεῦγος τρυγόνων ἢ δύο νεοσσοὺς περιστερῶν' which is rendered in English as 'a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons'.

The Greek contains the direct quotation 'Γυνή, ἥ τις ἐὰν σπερματισθῇ καὶ τέκῃ ἄρσεν, ἑπτὰ ἡμέρες ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται' which is rendered in English as 'a woman who conceives and bears a male is unclean for seven days'.
The Greek contains the direct quotation 'Ἐὰν δὲ τέκῃ θῆλυ, δὶς ἑπτὰ ἀκάθαρτος ἔσται' which is rendered in English as 'if a woman gives birth to a female, she is unclean for twice seven days'.

The Greek contains the phrases 'ἡ βακτηρία τῆς ἀπάτης, ἡ χειραγωγὸς τῆς παρακοῆς, ἡ τοῦ δράκοντος σύμβουλος, τὸ συντετριμμένον κεράμιον' which describe Eve's symbolic role as the source of frailty and are translated as 'the bacteria of the disease, the hand of disobedience, the counselor of the dragon, and broken pottery'.
